use_case: Track and equipment defect detection (computer vision): cameras on 3 hi-rail inspection vehicles and 2 wayside machine vision portals flag suspected track defects (joint bars, fasteners, ties, rail surface) and visible car component defects for human review
business_owner: Chief Engineer (track); Chief Mechanical Officer (portal car flags)
vendor_or_model: Defect detection vendor: licensed computer vision model run as an inference service in the company's corporate workloads cloud account; images in the company's image store
data_categories: Images and video of track, bridges, signal equipment, grade crossings, and passing rail cars, including PIH tank cars; GPS and milepost; inspector review decisions. Incidental images of employees, trespassers, and the public at crossings
affects_individuals: Yes (indirectly: crews, roadway workers, and the public depend on track and equipment safety; incidental images of people)
human_in_the_loop: A qualified track inspector designated under 49 CFR 213.7 reviews every track flag and still performs every required visual inspection; portal car flags go to a qualified mechanical inspector before departure. The model never clears a defect, sets or removes a slow order, or closes an inspection
applicable_laws: 49 CFR 213.233(b) (inspection devices only supplement visual inspection); 49 CFR 213.7; 49 CFR 215.13; 49 CFR part 211 (any change to inspection frequency would need an FRA waiver; none sought); 49 CFR 1520.9 if imagery reveals security measures; Fla. Stat. 501.171 not triggered (no names linked to images)
status: In production on the hi-rail vehicles since 2025-06 and the portals since 2026-01; approved with conditions 2026-09-15; expansion to the branch lines on hold

use_case: Locomotive predictive maintenance analytics: telemetry from 52 road locomotives is scored by a vendor model that predicts traction motor, air compressor, and cooling system failures and suggests shop work
vendor_or_model: Locomotive telemetry and analytics vendor (machine learning models in the vendor's cloud; read-only telemetry gateway on each locomotive)
data_categories: Locomotive sensor data, fault codes, GPS; maintenance history. No personal data except the engineer ID in event recorder fields, which the gateway does not send
affects_individuals: Indirectly (train crews rely on locomotive condition)
consequential_decision_category: None (maintenance planning); re-tier to Safety/CI if used to defer a repair or set an inspection interval
human_in_the_loop: Mechanical supervisors decide all shop work; daily (49 CFR 229.21) and periodic (229.23) inspections are unchanged; the model cannot defer a defect found by an inspector
applicable_laws: 49 CFR 229.21 and 229.23 (inspections and repairs unchanged; the analytics are not used to set inspection intervals); C-TRANSPORTATION-R01 (SD 1580/82-2022-01E III.B.2.b) for the gateway path
status: In production since 2024-11; approved with conditions 2026-09-15

use_case: Applicant screening in the HR applicant tracking system: a vendor feature scores and ranks applicants for conductor trainee, track laborer, and mechanical positions against the job posting
vendor_or_model: Applicant tracking system vendor (machine learning ranking feature turned on by vendor default in 2026-02)
data_categories: Resumes, application answers, work history, education, location; voluntary self-identification data held separately for EEO reporting
affects_individuals: Yes (job applicants: about 2,400 applications from 2026-02 to 2026-08)
human_in_the_loop: Recruiters review every application today, but they worked the ranked list from the top; ranking switched off 2026-09-01 until the conditions are met
applicable_laws: Title VII disparate impact (42 U.S.C. 2000e-2(k)); Uniform Guidelines on Employee Selection Procedures (29 CFR part 1607, including the four-fifths rule in 1607.4(D)); ADA (42 U.S.C. 12112(b)(6)); Florida Civil Rights Act (Fla. Stat. 760.10)
status: Ranking paused 2026-09-01; reinstatement only after the adverse impact analysis and conditions in the assessment

use_case: Enterprise generative AI assistant for drafting, summarizing, and searching company documents
vendor_or_model: Enterprise generative AI assistant under a company agreement (no training on company data; company-controlled retention; SSO with MFA)
data_categories: Internal and Restricted business documents permitted; SSI and credentials not permitted
human_in_the_loop: Users review all outputs before use; no output is sent to a regulator, customer, or partner without human review
applicable_laws: 49 CFR 1520.9(a) (SSI only to covered persons with a need to know); POL-04 4.11; POL-05 4.8
status: In production for 120 users since 2026-05; rollout to all office users by 2027-03-31 with public tools blocked

use_case: Shipper portal chatbot: answers shippers' questions about car status, demurrage, and service, using the logged-in shipper's car data
business_owner: Director of Customer Service and Car Management
vendor_or_model: Chatbot vendor (large language model with a retrieval layer over the portal's car data)
data_categories: Shipper contact details; car numbers, locations, and commodity data for the logged-in shipper, including hazmat flags
consequential_decision_category: None (information); hazmat questions are handed to staff
human_in_the_loop: Answers are automated, but the chatbot discloses that it is AI, cannot change orders or bills, and hands hazmat, billing disputes, and RSSM questions to customer service staff
applicable_laws: FTC Act Section 5 (truthful representations); 49 CFR 1520.9 (no SSI in the knowledge base); shipper contract confidentiality
status: In production since 2026-04; approved with conditions 2026-09-15
